canal_p12_001.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_001.text: On the twenty-seventh morning, Yue returned to the house beside the spill with a folded ground map and the gardener's empty bean jar. The grandmother took the jar as if the return mattered more than the map. Her tenant's cooking shelf had moved higher during the owner's separately paid fitting, and the millet replacement sat in a dry sack above it. The private settlement had changed a room. Outside, the clay dip still pointed toward the yard, waiting for the canal's first low-flow question.

canal_p12_002.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_002.text: The owner had invited her older son to the visit because he repaired ordinary household shutters. He arrived carrying a saw and wanted to raise the entire yard wall before any water moved. Bao asked him to compare the present spill guide and private outlet first. A higher wall might trap ordinary drainage against the house. The son thought every caution hid a refusal to help. Yue watched him measure the doorway with the saw handle, trying to make a visible answer from the tool he already understood.

canal_p12_003.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_003.text: The grandmother told him the grain shelf was useful and the spill plan still worried her. He wanted her to stay with his family upriver until the term ended. She wanted to remain near her own hearth unless actual warning required departure. Their argument had rehearsed itself before Yue arrived. The owner asked whether they could walk the current higher route together instead of deciding everything at the doorway. The grandmother agreed. Her son put down the saw as if abandoning a small but loyal ally.

canal_p12_004.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_004.text: The orchard-wall bench stood outside the soft hollow, reached by the checked public strip. The grandmother walked there with her light covered sack and paused once to breathe. Her son carried nothing because she had refused to hand the sack over. Yue wanted to offer help when the woman stopped, but waited until she asked for the bench cloth from her pouch. The real route took longer than the first arrow on the drawing. Luo adjusted the expected warning interval to the actual slower walk.

canal_p12_005.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_005.text: At the bench, the grandmother said she could leave if she knew why the call came. A shouted word from the canal might sound like ordinary cargo business. Luo asked where a nearer spoken relay could stand on sound ground during any accepted lower trial. The owner offered the outer gate corner without admitting workers into the house. The position could see the upper call and speak clearly toward the yard. Yue drew its sight lines and asked the grandmother to tell them which ordinary voices she could hear from her cooking place.

canal_p12_006.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_006.text: The son wanted a bell fixed directly above the doorway. Luo had brought no new bell circuit or paid keeper for one. She could arrange the existing spoken relay for a planned trial and seek a separately funded warning response if high water threatened later. The grandmother preferred a person naming the actual need rather than an unfamiliar bell frightening her while she cooked. Her son looked frustrated by how slowly a plan formed when the person being protected had preferences of her own.

canal_p12_007.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_007.text: Bao checked the repaired crossing lip and small household-close board before the low-flow visit. The guide timber stayed seated on its current dry support, and the ordinary private drainage path remained clear below it. He marked the test's lowest safe closing position on the handle. The board would control only its small crossing at the checked head. It could not hold back a flood bearing on the whole hollow. Yue kept that limit on the operator's sheet while the son wandered toward his abandoned saw.

canal_p12_008.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_008.text: The current trial would use a measured low feed while the upper observer watched the pocket and lower observers watched the crossing and basin. The whole lower route remained outside flood acceptance; today's question concerned visible low-flow behavior after the dry repair. The pilot had brought the team's ordinary survey passage, and the landing receiver held cargo clear for the short agreed interval. No powered frame would be used. Jiang's original appointment was complete, and the workshop's fresh standby remained an unaccepted quote.

canal_p12_009.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_009.text: The gardener arrived carrying a full basket and stood exactly where Bao had placed a new observation mark. He said it was the natural place to put beans while waiting. Bao moved the mark onto another sound spot with the same clear sight line, keeping the working retreat open. The man accepted the change without an argument. Yue had expected him to be difficult because yesterday he had been. Today a small reasonable request let him remain a gardener rather than spend the morning proving he opposed the canal.

canal_p12_010.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_010.text: The reed gatherer came from his temporary shed after checking his own cutter's storage. He accepted a short local-guide task within a formally exchanged unstarted observation interval. Its wage and ending time were written before the trial. He would watch the basin return from sound ground and call any unexpected route. The original repair labor stayed within its remaining accepted hours. He said he liked a job whose description admitted that he could leave afterward. Luo handed him the actual sheet, and he read it before signing.

canal_p12_011.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_011.text: Pei's counter message arrived with the scheduled boat. The offered reference matched the scratched-through line's exterior number and season. The chosen name Qiao Lan could be restored through the attribution amendment after the niece's agreed home reading. The collective two hundred forty days stayed unchanged. Yue gave the niece the approved comparison rather than posting the name at the garden landing. The aunt had asked to hear it at home first. A found line could wait a few more hours to reach its owner properly.

canal_p12_012.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_012.text: The grandmother listened to that news and said she remembered Qiao Lan making a song about a worker's missing shoe. Her son wanted to know what the story had to do with leaving a flood yard. She said she had been answering another person's question before he was born. He fell quiet, ashamed of his impatience. Yue wrote no lesson beside that exchange. The woman had a history beyond being old enough to worry them, and a morning could contain more than one useful subject.

canal_p12_013.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_013.text: Before the test, Bao asked everyone to take the actual ground route again. The grandmother would remain in her ordinary safe yard during the bounded low feed, with the owner beside her; any planned departure rehearsal would occur with the feed closed. The son wanted to stand near the moving board. His household tool experience did not qualify him as its operator. He accepted the viewing place after Luo showed him the clear line. He could watch useful work without joining its most dangerous part to prove he cared.

canal_p12_014.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_014.text: Yue held the field sheet at the crossing observer's spot and found the inner ruling too small for quick wet-weather reading. She rewrote the essential marks on a larger plain sheet, leaving detailed figures in the cover. The reed gatherer said he could read the simple words from his own position without moving closer. Bao checked both copies against the same actual limits. Neatness was useful until it made a person squint toward a place she should not enter. Yue tied the large sheet above the ordinary splash reach.

canal_p12_015.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_015.text: Luo gave the first hand-feed call after current head and ground checks. The upper operator admitted the limited water while the lower stop opened only to its planned test notch. A thin stream ran along the reinstated entrance and reached the guide lip. The gardener stopped joking. Yue could hear the change in everyone's breathing before she saw the first water edge turn toward the public outer strip. Bao watched the crossing mark, and the owner watched her ordinary outlet rather than the most attractive stream.

canal_p12_016.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_016.text: Water reached the shallow spreader in several separate threads. The reed gatherer called the first basin arrival from his sound position. The private outlet remained open, with no backing at the yard's marked low point. Yue wanted to declare success. Bao asked for the next current reading. The gardener then called that water was gathering beside a bean stake outside the intended strip. Luo closed the feed at once. The spill had not become a flood, but the actual line had already found something their dry shaping missed.

canal_p12_017.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_017.text: The bean stake stood on a low pocket hidden by yesterday's loose soil. A small trickle had followed a shallow seam into it and stopped short of the planted row. The gardener insisted the row would have been lost if they kept feeding. Bao said the observed low trickle justified the stop; today's view did not measure a larger future loss. Yue wrote both the actual wet limit and his offered concern. The man wanted the concern visible. She read his sentence aloud until he accepted the words.

canal_p12_018.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_018.text: With feed closed, the limited water drained through the checked basin return while observers kept their positions. The upper stop closed by its ordinary geared mechanism; no stone supply was drawn. Bao would examine the side seam after the ground stopped carrying visible flow. The grandmother watched from the yard and asked whether the stop meant she should leave. The nearer relay told her plainly that the planned trial had stopped for a small route correction, and the actual departure call had not been given.

canal_p12_019.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_019.text: The son wanted to dig a trench around the bean bed himself. Bao asked him to wait for the observed seam check because an extra trench might pull water toward the house outlet. He put his saw down again, now with less theatrical frustration. The gardener said nobody needed a saw to change his beans. The son laughed reluctantly. Their irritation found a shared absurdity that made waiting possible. Yue looked at the two men and wondered how much practical work depended on one useful laugh at the right moment.

canal_p12_020.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_020.text: The low-flow report kept the private outlet's successful current behavior separate from the missed side seam. The upper pocket and manual response had worked within the trial's actual limits. The lower spreader needed reshaping before another feed. The clear ground route remained useful. Bao sketched a small shoulder of compacted material inside the public strip to guide the seam back toward the basin, with its quantity drawn from the field repair's unspent finishing stock. The gardener checked that the shoulder would not move the wet boundary into his ordinary path.

canal_p12_021.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_021.text: The owner asked whether today's successful outlet observation meant she could forget the close board. Luo said the little board still had its own inspection and ordinary hand procedure. The trial had shown a useful current state, not removed future maintenance. Yue heard the owner sigh at another duty. Bao offered the actual service schedule and the choice of a paid local receiver or the canal's appointed keeper under the agreed access terms. The owner chose the canal receiver rather than becoming an unpaid small-gate specialist because she happened to live nearby.

canal_p12_022.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_022.text: At noon, the grandmother served tea from her repaired kettle at its modest safe fill. Bao's temporary tie had been replaced by her ordinary repairer using the owner's personal payment. Yue noticed only because the handle sat at a different angle. The little household job had reached its actual conclusion without needing the canal meeting. The grandmother asked whether the plant from the gate had survived. Yue described Tian's firm new leaf and thought it good that the day's conversation still had space for something that did not control water.

canal_p12_023.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_023.text: The niece returned after reading Qiao Lan's corrected name to her aunt. The aunt approved the offered public attribution and both remembered sentences about singing and fatigue. Pei could now post the amendment at the canal with the family wording already heard at home. The niece brought no original paper away. She wanted a copy for a cousin, which the clerk could prepare on the ordinary next boat. Yue added the real small task without turning it into another reason to postpone the accepted low-flow correction.

canal_p12_024.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_024.text: Bao laid the shoulder material in shallow layers and checked its shape with the ordinary level staff. Yue helped measure the compacted surface from stable ground while the feed remained closed. The gardener kept the protected bean boundary visible using his own existing stakes. They did not raise a wall capable of trapping the whole hollow. The small shaping addressed the route that today's little water had actually taken. A future higher-head test would need its own conditions rather than an encouraging prediction about this dry afternoon.

canal_p12_025.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_025.text: Luo asked the current observers whether a repeated feed could fit their remaining accepted intervals tomorrow. The reed gatherer could return for the short morning already exchanged within his task. The owner's availability ended earlier because she had a market journey. The nearer relay could use the same sound outer corner under the recorded access arrangement while the tenant remained. The owner wanted an actual report sent to her market receiver before she heard another rumor. Yue wrote the route and time where everybody could see them.

canal_p12_026.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_026.text: The son chose to stay overnight after his mother invited him, bringing his saw indoors and doing the shutter repair he had come equipped to do. He had wanted to rebuild the bank because that sounded like protection. Fitting a shutter kept wind out of her sleeping room today. Yue watched him measure it with a proper household rule borrowed from the owner. His mother told him he could leave the decorative carving alone. He said she had never appreciated his artistic gifts. She said she remembered the crooked gifts very well.

canal_p12_027.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_027.text: Before the repeated trial, three remaining jobs could improve what the current plan had missed. Luo needed the spoken relay tested from the grandmother's actual cooking place, Bao needed the corrected shoulder compared with the private outlet levels, and the niece wanted help preparing Qiao Lan's approved copies for their chosen readers. The ordinary staff would bring every result to the landing. Yue could work on a call people had to hear, a route water had to follow or a restored name people had to read in their own time.

canal_p12_028.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_028.text: The afternoon sun dried the seam's visible edge while the repaired kettle cooled on the table. Yue felt less eager for a perfect second trial than she had before the first. The useful plan had changed because somebody watched from beside his beans, and because an older woman asked exactly what a stopping word meant. Tomorrow's low feed needed those changes carried into the actual positions. Tonight's tasks would be small, but leaving one unfinished could make the next water less understandable than the last.

canal_p12_029.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_029.text: Yue could check the nearer spoken call with Luo, help Bao compare the reshaped spill strip or carry the approved family attribution copies. The feed would remain closed while they worked. Each job could finish before the agreed boat and supper, with reports assembled by the current landing receiver. The grandmother's son had finally begun cutting the shutter to its measured width. The house sounded like ordinary work again, and Yue wanted the canal's next call to leave that ordinary life somewhere safe to continue.

choices.text: Check the nearer warning call with Luo.
Compare the repaired crossing with Bao.

canal_p12_030.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_030.text: Luo stood at the outer gate corner while Yue sat at the grandmother's cooking stool. The woman stirred a little barley in her pot and said this was where a warning had to find her, not at the bench where everyone listened politely. Luo called the planned trial stop in ordinary full words. Yue heard the first phrase but lost the reason beneath the rattling shutter the son was fitting. She reported that actual gap instead of guessing what she would hear after the repair finished.

canal_p12_031.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_031.text: The son stopped hammering for another call. This time Yue and the grandmother both heard Luo clearly. The test showed a voice that worked in quiet, but not one protected from ordinary household work. Luo asked whether the nearer relay could repeat from the corner's sheltered side, facing the yard more directly while keeping the upper observer in view. The grandmother agreed to the position outside her gate. Yue checked its sound from the stool after the hammering resumed, and the complete words carried better.

canal_p12_032.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_032.text: The departure call used a different full sentence naming the checked higher landing route. Luo spoke it during the dry rehearsal only, with every participant told beforehand that this was practice. The grandmother repeated what she would do: leave the pot, take the light sack if already at hand and walk toward the bench. Her son wanted her to promise to hurry. She said she could promise to leave, not become a younger woman because a word was urgent. Luo recorded the actual slower walking allowance they had measured.

canal_p12_033.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_033.text: After the rehearsal, the grandmother asked Yue to help choose what belonged in the light sack. There were grain, a little household medicine, a needle wrapper and a painted cup. Yue expected the food to take priority. The woman wanted the cup because her late husband had painted its uneven bird before they moved here. They weighed the modest sack by hand and kept the cup wrapped beside the medicine. An evacuation plan that forgot why a person wanted to return could be sound on paper and impossible in her heart.

canal_p12_034.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_034.text: The cup's bird had three legs because the painter misjudged the space and refused to scrape it back. Yue laughed after the grandmother did. Her son said his father had claimed it ran faster that way. The story had survived as a household joke even after the man died. Yue thought of all the strange objects she could have called clutter while clearing a path. This one fitted in the light sack. Respecting it required a little cloth, not making the whole departure slower than the checked route allowed.

canal_p12_035.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_035.text: Luo tested the relay's view toward the upper call again after shifting its position. A hanging seed cover now cut across the sight line. The owner agreed to move it during any accepted live interval, then put it back afterward. The change stayed on the local task sheet. Nobody acquired a permanent right to rearrange the household because one afternoon's hearing worked better. Yue tied the cover's temporary hook at the offered spot and checked that the son could still finish his shutter without catching it.

canal_p12_036.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_036.text: At the gate corner, the reed gatherer came to hear the full stop and departure phrases. His own basin call would be relayed by the upper operator as needed; the house's nearer voice had a particular purpose and clear receiver. He asked whether he should leave his measuring position to help the grandmother if warning came. Luo said the ground response team would handle that need, and his first duty was the observed water call followed by his own retreat. The grandmother said she would rather hear the route than lose his warning in kindness.

canal_p12_037.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_037.text: They walked the dry departure path with the light sack again while the feed stayed closed. The grandmother paused at the bench, then completed the higher landing route at her own pace. Her son walked beside her without seizing the sack. Yue carried nothing and watched the ordinary footing. One loose apron stone clicked under the woman's boot. Luo marked it for the current path receiver, who could reseat it before tomorrow's live interval. The route gained another small repair because somebody walked it as a person rather than drawing a faster arrow.

canal_p12_038.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_038.text: The path receiver reseated the loose stone and checked its neighboring edge during his already accepted inspection interval. The grandmother tried the place once more and said it felt steady. Her son asked whether she would stay with him after the larger review. She said they could discuss that when today's rehearsal was finished. He accepted the answer and helped fold the bench cloth. Yue had seen him become more useful by asking smaller questions he could actually hear answered.

canal_p12_039.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_039.text: At the landing, Luo delivered the revised relay position, full spoken phrases and actual slower departure interval. Yue added the reseated apron stone and the light sack's agreed arrangement without listing the household's private objects. The grandmother kept her cup and medicine indoors until needed. Tomorrow's trial would use the checked call; a future warning would still require actual current conditions and response staff. The house now had words that meant two different actions, heard from a real stool rather than imagined from the path.

canal_p12_040.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_040.text: Bao laid the level staff beside the corrected shoulder while Yue held its base on stable paving. The gardener watched from his own dry rows, suspicious that the new guide would steal more of his picking path than their drawing promised. Bao compared the actual width at three points. The middle point had grown broader while the shallow layers were compacted. Yue marked it, and Bao trimmed that small shoulder edge back inside the agreed strip before the test. A straight sketch did not guarantee a straight shovel.

canal_p12_041.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_041.text: The trimmed material stayed in the ordinary finishing stock instead of being thrown over the private row. The gardener said his father would have accepted a narrower path if the bank simply asked politely. Bao asked whether his father ever carried this particular basket. The man laughed and said the old man's baskets were smaller. Yue drew the actual walking width beside the service line. The current agreement concerned bodies and loads present today, which made a remembered easier ancestor less useful than a measured basket.

canal_p12_042.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_042.text: At the crossing, the private outlet's cleaned cover remained seated under its proper support. Bao checked the accessible lip height without opening the buried pipe again merely for reassurance. The owner's marked ordinary flow had left no new backing in her yard. Yue read the height aloud while he wrote it on the larger observer sheet. She liked knowing a number before somebody else corrected it. Then he asked her to check the staff's footing, and she saw a little stone lifting its base away from the intended reference.

canal_p12_043.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_043.text: She reset the staff on the clean fixed mark and repeated the reading. The new figure matched the actual outlet plan within its accepted tolerance. Her first figure stayed crossed out in the field record with its displaced footing noted. The gardener said the stone had tried to raise the house. Yue said it had briefly raised her confidence too. Bao smiled, then asked for the last crossing level. Humor made the correction easier without allowing the inaccurate first height to remain the one somebody used.

canal_p12_044.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_044.text: They inspected the guide's outer edge where the first trickle had found the side seam. The shallow seam now joined the public spreader instead of the bean-stake pocket. Bao wanted another small bucket comparison with the feeder closed before tomorrow's larger low feed. The limited ordinary bucket water would enter only the corrected reachable surface, with the observer at its safe mark. Yue fetched the measured container from the assigned store and waited for the actual call instead of conducting the interesting little test while Bao walked elsewhere.

canal_p12_045.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_045.text: The bucket's small stream followed the new shoulder and reached the spreader without touching the dry bean stake. Bao accepted that observation and kept its limited volume distinct from the proposed feed trial. The gardener wanted him to say the beans were safe now. Yue read the actual observation rather than the wider promise. The man sighed and said he disliked people who came with good news and then made it smaller. Bao told him the small good news was something they could repeat tomorrow.

canal_p12_046.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_046.text: The reed basin's return stayed clear after the recovered fish trap left. Bao checked the spreader's far lip from its marked dry position. A loose reed bunch lay against the channel entrance, dropped during the gatherer's move. Its owner recovered it with an ordinary hook before any flow, then retied the bundle above the path. He looked annoyed with himself. Yue had enough recent mistakes to avoid sounding superior. She thanked him for moving it now, and he laughed that he had finally found work cleaning up his own convenience.

canal_p12_047.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_047.text: At the public strip's narrow turn, Yue compared the current sketch with the planted rows and saw how a careless copy could send the next observer to the wrong side. She redrew the turn using the fixed wall and bean stakes as visible landmarks, without treating private movable stakes as permanent survey references. Bao checked the final picture. The simple observer map became easier to follow than the exact level sheet. They would keep both because different kinds of work needed different kinds of accuracy.

canal_p12_048.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_048.text: The owner looked over the corrected crossing figures before leaving for her morning market journey. She accepted the current dry changes and kept the next live observation conditional on its actual limits. Bao gave her the report receiver's time and the route for a stopping message from the yard. She asked Yue whether the bank found her troublesome. Yue said the first low water had made trouble before she did. The owner laughed and packed her seed parcel for market. The answer left her concern inside the work rather than outside it.

canal_p12_049.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_049.text: At the landing, Bao submitted the corrected shoulder dimensions, repeated level and small bucket result. Yue kept the displaced-staff correction visible in the exact field notes. The gardener accepted that the planned repeat would watch his bean boundary again. The bucket had supported a modest repair; it had not certified flood behavior. Yue washed the clay from her hands and felt pleased by a useful observation that belonged to ordinary water and ordinary ground. The larger questions could wait until they had a real test rather than a prettier sentence.

canal_p12_050.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_050.text: The niece carried the approved attribution copy in a clean household wrapper. Yue walked with her to the aunt's house before the evening boat. Qiao Lan's chosen name stood in the broad public form, no longer buried under the scratched household move. The aunt touched the exterior reference and said she wanted one copy kept in the old tin beside the original counterfoil. The corrected acknowledgment would join the family's existing paper rather than replace what made its recovery possible.

canal_p12_051.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_051.text: The aunt asked Yue to read the two offered memory sentences. Qiao Lan had enjoyed making workers laugh with the song, and had come home exhausted after the turns. The niece wanted to shorten them into a sweeter public line. Her aunt refused, kindly but firmly. She had offered both because both belonged to her sister. Yue kept the approved wording unchanged. A restored name could still become someone else's decoration if the next writer decided affection required smoothing its difficult edge.

canal_p12_052.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_052.text: One cousin wanted a copy because his own work token came from a different household move. The aunt warned him that this reference would not certify his separate history. He knew and wanted to compare how the form recorded a chosen name. Yue arranged the requested copy with its actual limitation. He described the clerk who always shortened his mother's name without asking. The conversation found another current use for the amendment without pretending that one recovered counterfoil had solved every name on the bank.

canal_p12_053.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_053.text: The niece offered to read the corrected name at the garden landing before supper. Her aunt approved after the private home reading was complete. Yue asked whether the aunt wanted the personal song story read there too. She preferred to leave those sentences for the later public history, where its context could stay beside the founding burden. The landing reading would name the recovered person and accepted seasonal reference. The smaller announcement felt sufficient because the owner of the offered story had chosen its size.

canal_p12_054.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_054.text: At the landing, the niece stood on the ordinary dry step and read Qiao Lan's corrected acknowledgment. The gardener stopped tying his basket and listened. He said his father had mentioned a woman with that name who could repair a rope's frayed cover. His memory would need its own source if later used in a history. Today it was simply a man remembering something after hearing a name again. The niece thanked him and continued with the actual seasonal reference, keeping the approved public statement clear.

canal_p12_055.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_055.text: A child asked whether the dead woman had built the entire canal. Yue said the acknowledgment concerned her recorded completed turns inside a collective season, not every piece of timber along the water. The niece said she would have found the question funny. The child looked disappointed that old people did not always become legendary when someone found their papers. His grandmother said legends never washed their own bowls. Yue laughed and gave the child's next practical question about tomorrow's test to the actual keeper.

canal_p12_056.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_056.text: The evening boat could take the approved public comparison to Pei and bring the cousin's requested copy on its next ordinary route. Yue checked the actual cover and receiver with the pilot, paying no imaginary special courier fee out of the repair order. The ordinary public document carriage already belonged to the operations schedule. The niece kept her own home copy. A recovered name now traveled through chosen ordinary hands, which seemed a better future than lying forever in a clerk's grand speech about rediscovery.

canal_p12_057.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_057.text: The aunt's house had an old work song written on a cooking wall in faint charcoal. She let the niece copy the verses she could still read, but asked for its missing lines to remain missing rather than borrowed from a newer market version. Yue heard the beginning sung softly while the supper pot warmed. The tune moved slowly, with a rest where somebody could have raised a beam or simply caught her breath. Yue wished Tian could hear it and asked whether the aunt would permit that later.

canal_p12_058.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_058.text: The aunt agreed to a copied tune brought to Tian as a personal offering, with its known gaps kept visible. It would not be evidence for a new labor claim. The niece made the copy on her own spare sheet after finishing the public papers. Yue asked her to use the known ordinary boat route, and she accepted that small delivery. The older woman smiled and said the easiest gifts were sometimes the ones people finally managed to bring.

canal_p12_059.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_059.text: At the landing, Yue gave the clerk's receiver the approved attribution and left the personal tune in the niece's chosen delivery cover. The niece would return home before supper rather than remain for every canal discussion. Qiao Lan's public name could now be restored, its exterior reference matching the accepted collective season. Yue had watched a family decide how much of its dead sister's story should enter the world. The choice gave the recovered line more dignity than the speed with which an eager apprentice might have announced it.

canal_p12_060.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_060.text: The afternoon results met at the landing before the return passage. The nearer relay could be heard from the actual cooking place, the reshaped shoulder and crossing levels had their corrected field record, and Qiao Lan's public attribution had passed its requested home reading. The personal tune kept its chosen delivery route. Yue heard the work she had not followed from those who completed it. Tomorrow's low feed could use these real changes without imagining she had been present at every place the bank now depended on.

canal_p12_061.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_061.text: Luo checked the night relay plan with the ordinary keeper replacement before leaving. No current flood warning had been issued; the spoken positions belonged to tomorrow's planned trial. The grandmother kept her light sack ready without abandoning her own hearth tonight. Her son finished the shutter and tested its latch from both sides. Yue heard its firm ordinary click while they said goodbye. The sound was more comforting than his morning claim that he could raise every wall before dark.

canal_p12_062.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_062.text: On the twenty-eighth morning, the owner departed for market after receiving the current trial report route. The tenant remained, and the nearer relay took the accepted outer-corner position. The reed gatherer's short basin task began at its recorded time. Bao checked the shoulder and guide after the dry night, while Luo read the actual feeder head. The current low-feed limit stayed below the upper pocket's accepted twenty-centimetre maximum. They could ask the lower route another small question without pretending the first stopped feed had never happened.

canal_p12_063.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_063.text: The limited water reached the reshaped shoulder and turned into the public spreader. Yue watched the bean stake while the gardener watched it too, each from the sound dry side. No trickle entered its low pocket this time. The private outlet continued running without backing into the yard. The basin receiver called the actual arrival and return. Bao asked for the final current crossing mark, and Yue gave the observed reading rather than the number she knew would make his drawing look right.

canal_p12_064.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_064.text: The trial ended at its planned interval with the feed closed by Luo's ordinary hand mechanism. The bounded volume drained through the checked return; no apparatus charge was spent. The witness marks remained seated, and the actual observed low route stayed inside its repaired strip. Bao accepted this low-flow behavior under today's head and conditions. He preserved the first stop and shoulder correction in the final report. The report did not grant flood acceptance simply because the second little stream had pleased everyone standing beside it.

canal_p12_065.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_065.text: The gardener asked whether he should remove the bean stake now that it no longer watched a leak. Bao asked him to keep his ordinary crop boundary intact while using a separate fixed survey mark for later checks. The man laughed and said he preferred a stake with only one employer. He took his basket to market, leaving the rows dry. Yue watched him go without requesting a statement of support for common water. His actual agreement had survived contact with a corrected stream; that was already something worth keeping.

canal_p12_066.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_066.text: The grandmother's son walked with her to the resting bench after the feed closed, practicing the actual departure route once more. He carried the empty jar while she held the light sack. She rested at the bench, then said she would stay in the house until a real warning changed the plan. He accepted that choice and asked her to visit his family afterward if she wanted. The invitation sounded different when it no longer tried to disguise an order. Yue looked away to give their small agreement room.

canal_p12_067.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_067.text: The reed gatherer received his accepted task wage against the formally exchanged observation hours. He returned to his higher temporary shed before the ending time moved into another unpaid question. The ordinary repair labor line remained finite, and the report listed its actual completed hours. Bao had later field checking within his changed allocation; any larger response required separate funding. Yue had learned to hear these limits without imagining they drained all feeling from the work. The gatherer's relief at leaving on time had feeling enough.

canal_p12_068.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_068.text: At the canal, Pei posted Qiao Lan's corrected personal attribution after the family's approved reading. The chosen name stood beside the accepted exterior reference, with the collective seasonal total unchanged. The old scratched line stayed visible beneath the amendment. Tian came to look while waiting for a customer's cloth. She asked Yue whether the recovered woman had enjoyed the work. Yue gave both offered memory sentences. The family had also arranged a separate permitted tune through the niece's ordinary route, where affection could travel outside the public record.

canal_p12_069.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_069.text: By evening, the aunt's niece had sent the permitted tune copy directly to Tian through the ordinary garden boat. Its gaps stayed visible. Tian tried the first verse while winding thread and laughed at the missing shoe. She did not use the song to praise inherited duty. A woman who had worked, joked and grown tired could be remembered beside people choosing their own present jobs. Yue listened without asking the tune to settle the canal, then helped hold a length of paid thread while Tian wound its stubborn end.

canal_p12_070.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_070.text: Han showed Luo his actual week's gear observations after the lock closed. The reduced crane and private landing platforms had provided useful service within their current limits. The proposed later lease still needed the closing decision, and the valid fifty-six claim remained under its toll terms. The private hoist and four planks stood tagged for the cooper's fortieth-day delivery. Tian joked that everything Han owned now seemed to have a later date attached. He said her next sail bill looked much the same from his side of the counter.

canal_p12_071.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_071.text: On the twenty-ninth morning, Bao and the keeper replacement checked the ordinary gate's cap marks. The fastening remained seated after more paid traffic. The household drain stayed clear, and its removable lid could actually be found without shifting a loaded platform. Those earlier repairs had continued serving while Yue visited the lower route. She copied the current readings beside the new field report. A novel week could distract an apprentice from old obligations; the ordinary receiver's repeated check kept the bank from forgetting whichever job no longer felt interesting.

canal_p12_072.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_072.text: The landing guild sent a preliminary answer to Luo's emergency request. A separately authorized thirty-six-copper response allocation could cover eight worker-day equivalents at three copper, eight for material and four for two additional charged stones if an actual higher-water warning justified the call. The guild had not yet released the money. Luo would present the current exposed route and workshop quote at its scheduled thirtieth-day meeting. The bank could plan the bounded possible response now without hiring Jiang on funds that existed only in an encouraging letter.

canal_p12_073.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_073.text: Yue read the proposed emergency task list and asked whether the people below the fork would get a named ground response before any larger live operation. Luo said the current request included it and would show the actual receiver when funded. Bao wanted the additional two stones retained for powered work only within checked apparatus conditions. They would not turn a flood into an available charging source. Yue put the proposal in the future-work cover and returned to her ordinary practice, grateful that the plan had a place for courage without pretending it came free.

canal_p12_074.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_074.text: The grandmother sent a message thanking Bao for the low-flow report arriving at her owner's actual market receiver. The owner had returned knowing what happened, instead of needing to choose between the tenant's worry and a passing rumor. She wanted the next high-water discussion at the house landing, where both could attend. Luo agreed to deliver any current warning through the actual nearer route. Yue saw an ordinary report repair part of a household conversation the hydraulic work alone could never have touched.

canal_p12_075.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_075.text: Tian sold another small stitching order and bought a pot that did not wobble for the gate seedling. The plant had held its new leaf and lost an old one. She put it on the flour-store stair long enough to show Yue, then took it home before somebody made it the bank's public mascot. Yue laughed and asked to borrow the stable pot's shape for a little sketch. Tian permitted a sketch, not the plant. A friendship had grown strong enough for such small limits to sound like ease.

canal_p12_076.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_076.text: A weather runner reached the lower landing near dusk. The upper ridge had steady rain after noon, with no present rise yet at the canal's checked marker. His note named the observer and the hour. Luo entered it beside the actual local reading and sent a message to the guild before tomorrow's meeting. The spill route had passed its small question, but the larger one was approaching from ground none of them could command. Yue carried the reading board indoors to protect its ink and felt the evening change around her.

canal_p12_077.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_077.text: Bao covered the exposed fitting surfaces and checked the ordinary retreat path before dark. The lower route remained empty after its bounded trial, with its current manual stops seated. Han moved his tagged private sale goods higher in the already dry store, taking his own precaution without charging it to public repair. The grandmother stayed in her house with the light sack ready. The reed gatherer slept in his accepted higher shed. The first steady rain note had arrived, and the bank finally had actual people attached to every place on its drawing.

canal_p12_078.speaker: narrator
canal_p12_078.text: Yue closed the low-flow report after supper and set her unpowered practice tile aside. Her arm pairs had stayed at their recovered earned stage throughout the ordinary field work. Tomorrow's guild meeting would decide whether the quoted emergency crew could be hired before the water rose. She listened to the keeper's ordinary gate call from below and remembered the grandmother's three-legged bird wrapped inside a light sack. A flood plan would be tested by how well it let people carry small lives toward higher ground.
